title: Coral and the Orchard
premise: Marine biologist Coral Reyes has spent eleven years building a life of careful distance on a small island research station, counting sea turtles and avoiding the hometown she fled after a betrayal she never explained. When a storm uncovers a letter her late grandmother never mailed—postmarked eleven years ago and revealing that Coral's departure cost someone else everything—she is forced back to the orchard town of Vesper Hollow, where Rafael Vane, the man she loved and abandoned without a word, now runs his family's failing cidery. As Coral works to restore the orchard's heritage apple trees, the only living link to her grandmother's secret, she and Rafael circle each other through grief, resentment, and rediscovered tenderness. When a rival developer threatens to bulldoze the orchard and Coral is offered the directorship of her dream research institute in another hemisphere, she must finally choose between the career that saved her and the man who sees her clearly at last. In the end, Coral declines the institute, Rafael signs the orchard over to a community land trust, and they build something new together—a coastal conservation partnership rooted in both their worlds.
about_author: K. M. Iversen is the pen name of a former field researcher who traded tide charts for love stories set where land meets water. Having lived in island towns where everyone knows everyone's business, Iversen writes romances about people who mistake solitude for safety.

chapters.title: The Weight of Water
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. On Merrow Island, Coral counts nesting turtles and deflects her mentor's offer: directorship of a prestigious mainland institute, decision due in six weeks. A hurricane tears open her grandmother's old storage shed, revealing a sealed letter addressed to Rafael's mother. Emotional beat: restless unease beneath a controlled life.

chapters.title: Postmarked Eleven Years Ago
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The letter reveals Coral's grandmother secretly sold half the Vane orchard to cover Coral's university debts—and begged forgiveness for a betrayal that made Coral's flight necessary. Guilt propels Coral to Vesper Hollow unannounced. Emotional beat: shame cracking open old armor.

chapters.title: The Man in the Cider House
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Rafael, widowed three years and drowning in debt, finds Coral standing in his parents' orchard like a ghost. Their first conversation is all barbed politeness; he agrees to let her help with harvest only because he needs hands. Emotional beat: anger tangled with unfinished longing.

chapters.title: Grafting Season
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Working side by side grafting heirloom trees, Coral and Rafael fall into old rhythms—shared jokes, accidental touches. She hides the letter's contents; he hides the foreclosure notice from the bank. Emotional beat: warmth rekindling despite mutual guardedness.

chapters.title: What the Town Remembers
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. At the harvest festival, old neighbors greet Coral with suspicion; Rafael's sister Delia confronts Coral about the night she vanished, forcing Coral to admit she left because she believed Rafael had betrayed her first—a misunderstanding neither ever verified. Emotional beat: humiliation and the ache of wasted years.

chapters.title: The Developer's Offer
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. A resort developer offers Rafael enough to erase his debts—if he sells the orchard outright. That same night, Coral almost tells him about the letter but loses her nerve when he mentions how much her abandonment cost him. Emotional beat: temptation versus loyalty, silence compounding.

chapters.title: First Frost
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The letter's truth finally spills out during an argument in the cider house: the orchard was never fully Rafael's, and Coral's whole exile was built on a lie. He walks out. Alone, Coral opens her acceptance email from the institute. Emotional beat: devastation and the vertigo of choice.

chapters.title: Rootstock
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Rafael discovers his mother knew about the sale all along and chose silence to protect him—mirroring Coral's silence. He realizes he has been punishing Coral for a wound no one caused deliberately. He searches for her; she's already packed for the mainland. Emotional beat: grief turning into clarity.

chapters.title: The Last Ferry
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. At the dock, Rafael asks Coral not to go—not to choose him, but to choose honestly for once. Coral boards anyway, then spends a sleepless week realizing the institute is another form of hiding. She calls Delia, learns the developer's deadline is tomorrow, and turns her ferry around. Emotional beat: courage arriving late but arriving.

chapters.title: Coral and the Orchard
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Coral returns as the developer's crew arrives; together she and Rafael rally the town, secure a community land trust using her institute connections, and save the orchard. She declines the directorship to launch a coastal conservation program based in Vesper Hollow. In spring, they plant a new tree where the shed once stood. Emotional beat: homecoming, truth chosen over safety, love rooted at last.
